text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More than 1,500 officers of the Nigerian police force have been transferred to different parts of the country in a major reorganisation.
- Petroleum Trust Fund agrees to provide 632 million naira for rehabilitation of water supplies in southwestern city of Ibadan.

- Central bank will impose a levy of 5,000 naira for every box of currency returned by a commercial bank which has not been sorted into reusable and unusable notes. A box contains roughly 300,000 naira.

- Fears are growing for the safety of an investment by Nigeria's Unipetrol in Sierra Leone's oil refinery. Nigeria's military government has called on the army rulers in Freetown to step down and return the civilian president.
- Nigeria's oil joint-venture partners are planning investments of about 408 billion naira in exploration and production for 1998, even though they are facing a funding crisis this year.
- Nigeria may privatise mining concessions and sell them off to the highest bidders.
- Nigeria may have lost about 700,000 barrels of condensate as a result of the temporary closure of the Oso condensate field, operated by Mobil Corp's local unit.
